title: Laws of Friction
theory:
**Big idea:** Four simple laws sum up how friction behaves between two solid bodies.

**The four laws**
1. **Slipping:** f_k = μ_k N, where μ_k is the coefficient of kinetic friction.
2. **Direction of kinetic friction:** opposite to the velocity of the body **relative to the body applying the friction**.
3. **No slipping:** f_s ≤ μ_s N. The direction and size of static friction are whatever is needed to prevent slipping.
4. **Area doesn't matter:** f_k and f_s do not depend on the area of contact, as long as N is the same.

**Some typical values of μ_s**
| Surfaces | μ_s (roughly) |
|---|---|
| Teflon on teflon | 0.04 (very slippery) |
| Ice on ice | 0.10 |
| Steel on steel | 0.58 |
| Rubber tyre on **wet** concrete | 0.7 |
| Rubber tyre on **dry** concrete | 1.0 |

These are rough estimates. The real value depends on smoothness, dust, oxide layers and other conditions.

**A surprise: clean copper**
Take two blocks of pure copper. Clean off all oxide and dust, heat out the dissolved gases, and press them together in a vacuum. They **stick**, and μ becomes **much larger than 1**. Let in a little air, a thin oxide layer forms, and μ drops back to normal values.

> 💡 This is why tyres grip less on a wet road: the water layer reduces μ_s.

> ⚠️ **Common misconception:** "A wider object has more friction." For the same weight (same N), the area of contact makes no difference.

questions.prompt: According to the laws of friction, for a given normal force the frictional force:

options.text: Increases with the area of contact
Decreases with the area of contact
Does not depend on the area of contact
Depends only on the speed

questions.explanation: The fourth law: friction is independent of the area of contact for the same N.

questions.prompt: When there is no slipping, the force of static friction:

options.text: Is always equal to μ_s N
Is less than or equal to μ_s N
Is always greater than μ_s N
Is always zero

questions.explanation: Static friction takes only the value needed, up to the maximum μ_s N.

questions.prompt: Which pair of surfaces has the **smallest** coefficient of static friction?

options.text: Teflon on teflon
Steel on steel
Rubber tyre on dry concrete
Rubber tyre on wet concrete

questions.explanation: Teflon on teflon (about 0.04) is extremely slippery.

questions.prompt: A rubber tyre grips a dry concrete road better than a wet one because:

options.text: The normal force is larger on a dry road
The area of contact is larger on a dry road
Wet roads have no friction at all
The coefficient of friction is larger for the dry road

questions.explanation: Typical values: about 1.0 on dry concrete and about 0.7 on wet.

questions.prompt: Two very clean blocks of pure copper pressed together in a vacuum:

options.text: Have almost zero friction
Stick, with a friction coefficient much larger than 1
Repel each other
Behave exactly as they would in air

questions.explanation: Without oxide and dust layers, the surfaces bond strongly.
